Guldmann ceiling lift track systems are proprietary and engineered to integrate directly with GH3+ motors. Other vendors’ track systems are incompatible with the motor mounting interfaces, load ratings, and software safety features required for proper GH3+ functionality. Use of a non-OEM track would: • render the VA-owned motors unusable, • void manufacturer warranties, • introduce unacceptable safety risks in patient-handling environments, and • necessitate purchasing new lift motors, resulting in substantial and avoidable additional costs. Q: Does the requirement mandate a 100% vendor-furnished rental model, or does SAVAHCS retain any existing Customer-Owned Linen Items (COLI) that the contractor will be required to process alongside rented inventory? A: A 100% vendor-furnished rental model. Q: If COLI processing is required, will the vendor be held liable for standard wear-and- tear or replacement costs for government-owned items? A: No. Q: What is the exact required Par level distribution across the health care system prior to Day 1 of contract performance (e.g., 3-Par, 4-Par, or 5-Par systemwide)? A: 3 Days. Q: What is the breakdown of initial Par stock required on-site at the SAVAHCS main campus versus off-site reserve? A: Off Site Reserve will be 96 hour contingency linen. Q: Will the VA provide an explicit physical technical specification sheet (e.g., thread count, GSM weight, fabric blend 55 / 45 cotton-poly vs. 100% barrier poly, color coding, surgical drape fluid-resistance ratings) for each line item? A: Fabric blend 55 / 45 cotton-poly vs. 100% barrier poly, color coding depending on the cost. 36C26227Q0001 Page 5 of 11 Q: Are micro-fiber mop heads, microfiber cloths, and barrier isolation gowns included in the general 1,350,000 lbs annual estimated volume, or are they counted / tracke

requirements, and designated delivery time slots for each satellite location. A: N/A. Q: Is the contractor required to supply all clean / soiled exchange carts, poly-dump carts, and wire delivery hampers? A: Contractor is required to supply all clean / soiled exchange carts. 36C26227Q0001 Page 6 of 11 Q: What are the physical dimensional constraints (height, width, depth) of the SAVAHCS logistics staging area, freight elevators, and clean linen rooms to ensure incoming contractor carts fit properly? A: Average dock dimensions for 24-foot box truck. Q: What is the minimum quantity of dedicated exchange carts required to remain on-site at SAVAHCS at all times? A: 30. Q: Is contractor performance restricted strictly to dock-to-dock exchange, or is the contractor responsible for internal ward-level replenishment / clean linen room stocking? A: Restricted strictly to dock-to-dock exchange. OBJECTIVE IRS-CI is seeking a vendor that can provide a base year plus four option years Indefinite Delivery/Quantity contract to fulfil mandatory ammunition requirements. This request is for the acquisition of duty and training ammunition for IRS-CI’s Special Agents. This request will fulfill the

rchase of duty and training ammunition for IRS-CI Special Agents to meet mandatory federal training program. OBJECTIVE IRS-CI is seeking a vendor that can provide a base year plus four option years Indefinite Delivery/Quantity contract to fulfil mandatory ammunition requirements. Variation in Estimated Quantity (Apr 1984) If the quantity of a unit-priced item in this contract is an estimated quantity and the actual quantity of the unit-priced item varies more than 15 percent above or below the estimated quantity, an equitable adjustment in the contract price shall be made upon demand of either party. The equitable adjustment shall be based upon any increase or decrease in costs due solely to the variation above 115 percent or below 85 percent of the estimated quantity. If the quantity variation is such as to cause an increase in the time necessary for completion, the Contractor may request, in writing, an extension of time, to be received by the Contracting Officer within 10 days from the beginning of the delay, or within such further period as may be Contract Title Solicitation No. H-4 granted by the Contracting Officer before the date of final settlement of the contract. "Native American" means of, or relating to, a tribe, people, or culture that is indigenous to the United States. "Sacred objects" means Native American items that are specific ceremonial objects needed by traditional Native American religious leaders for the practice of traditional Native American religions by their present-day adherents. These items are specifically limited to objects that were devoted to a traditional Native American religious ceremony or ritual and which have religious significance or function in the continued observance or renewal of such ceremony. "Objects of cultural patrimony" means Native American items having ongoing historical, traditional, or cultural importance central to the Native American tribe or Native Hawaiian organization itself, rather than property owned by an individual tribal or organization member. These objects are of such central importance that they may not be alienated, appropriated, or conveyed by any individual tribal or organization member. (b) General. Prior to an assessment, knowledge of the building systems and components present is necessary, since assessments are done against these components, not against the building as a whole. This information about the systems and components that make up a building is called the BUILDER Inventory. BUILDER has a vast library of predefined components which an assessor will select from, and the inventory collection process involves identifying the type, quantity, and year installed for all pertine nt components. These components are also organized into systems and sub-systems according to the UNIFORMAT classification hierarchy. When a specific instance of a component is recorded, this is called a component -section in BUILDER, and represents a single component assembly or collection of like components to be managed as a single unit.
